The stall watchdog is a reader of child file activity that the claims miss. /afk:investigate step 4 arms it over its tracers (skills/utils/investigate/SKILL.md:44), pointed at paths the child's work touches (DELEGATION.md:36), and it counts a child alive only while a file under those paths changes, exiting 3 after 20 idle minutes (hooks/stall-watchdog.sh:13-19, :23-24). A tracer that returns its fragment as text changes no such file, so the watchdog fires on a live tracer, and the task-output check of DELEGATION.md:37 is the only liveness signal left (inference).

/afk:execute Step 10.5 also reads the adversary report file. It remediates by each finding's class and, on adversary_fail, names each finding's class and repro path (skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:92, :118), while the ADVERSARY line it gets back carries only the verdict, the counts and the report path (skills/afk/adversary/SKILL.md:43) and the report is the child's only output (:51). So the findings reach execute through the file (inference).

/afk:understand is a reader of the adversary report that the claims miss: its feature mode reads {plan-dir}/review/*.md (skills/afk/understand/SKILL.md:49) and mines adversary reports for misconception callouts (skills/afk/understand/UNDERSTANDING-FORMAT.md:52).

The opt-in session block makes every session answer a code question by running /afk:investigate, 'plugin skill running or not' (skills/afk/setup/INVESTIGATION-SESSIONS.md:15-18). A spawned child whose session carries that block is one more agent that starts a run and writes a ledger itself; whether a subagent's session carries the block is harness runtime (B14).

The /afk:bug retester already sends its raw evidence back as text: it edits no file, not even a scratch file, and returns every command with its full output as its reply body (skills/afk/bug/RETEST-PROMPT.md:12, :21, :25); the main session, the only state.json writer, records the result (skills/afk/bug/SKILL.md:30, :88). It keeps writing only if a rendered page counts as a code or plugin-file edit; if it returns the markup instead, its starter holds the HTML (inference).

afk-implementor writes evidence files itself: 'Bulk evidence (logs, suite output) goes to a file' and its return carries the path (agents/afk-implementor.md:16). It is the type of the autopilot executor (skills/afk/autopilot/SKILL.md:35), of the settle-change fixers (skills/utils/settle-change/SKILL.md:57) and of the page writer (LAVISH.md:272).

No plugin hook can do the starter's write when a child returns. The shared hook events are SessionStart, PreToolUse and Stop (CAPABILITIES.md:26), both hook manifests register only those (hooks/hooks.json:3, :25, :53), and the native contract gate refuses any other event (hooks/native-contract-gate.sh:237-238). The write has to be a step in the starter's own prose (inference).

A starter that writes a returned ledger must reproduce the validated merge output exactly. The SDD gate and the plan validator re-validate the ledger they find (skills/afk/to-sdd/scripts/check_sdd_investigations.py:232; skills/afk/to-subtasks/scripts/validate_plan.py:476), and execute's ground diff compares each searched line by class, file and line_hash (skills/afk/execute/CITED-MODE.md:65). A summarized or truncated COVERAGE.json fails them (inference).

The agent that writes a ledger also names it: {spec-dir}/investigations/INV-NNN-slug/, with NNN the highest existing number plus one (skills/utils/investigate/LEDGER-FORMAT.md:14-18). Under the change a grill that writes the ledgers of its background set (skills/afk/grill-requirements/SKILL.md:46) allocates those numbers itself; the plan validator already refuses a number that resolves to two ledgers (skills/afk/to-subtasks/scripts/validate_plan.py:466-469) (inference).

The grounding rule keeps the grilling session's context on the interview while it acts on the ledgers (skills/afk/grill-solution/GROUNDING-RULE.md:40-43). If the grill must write each ledger its background runs return, each ledger's text enters that context (inference).

Five spawned children write no file today, so the change leaves them as they are: review's skeptics and dispute adjudicators return verdicts (skills/afk/review/SKILL.md:146; skills/afk/review/SETTLEMENT.md:17), /afk:understand's fresh skeptic returns a judgement (skills/afk/understand/SKILL.md:65), /afk:verify-seams' blind verifier is an afk-reader, which never creates a file (skills/utils/verify-seams/SKILL.md:17; agents/afk-reader.md:14), and /afk:settle-change's reviewer subagents return findings (skills/utils/settle-change/SKILL.md:14).

Under autopilot the adversary's starter is the executor subagent, not a root session: the review and adversary gates are spawned by the subtask's executing subagent (skills/afk/autopilot/SKILL.md:35). That executor may write only its Status cell, the MR checklist block and appends to JOURNAL.md and DECISIONS.md (skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:143), so writing plan/review/{NNNN-slug}-adversary.md for its child needs that rule changed (inference).

Mission control's adversary parsers read the first 4000 characters of each *-adversary.md and look for a 'verdict' word (skills/afk/mission-control/scripts/mc/sections/gates.py:21-25, :110-115; insights.py:204-209), while the adversary skill closes its report with the ADVERSARY line (skills/afk/adversary/SKILL.md:40-43). No mission-control test fixture carries an adversary report (skills/afk/mission-control/scripts/tests/test_contract.py:313-317), so this reader is unguarded whoever writes the file.

REPORTING.md:31 is a rule the claims miss. It makes a finding id legal only once its catalogue is on disk, and it lists the adversary report among those catalogues: 'enumerate, persist the catalogue, then refer'. Under the change the adversary returns before its starter writes the file, so a finding it names in its return has no catalogue on disk yet; that line does not say whether the return itself counts as one (inference).
